messages:
Sam D: Quick flag — PR #8992 (docs/pricing) contains a worked example that mixes list prices and applied discounts in a way that could confuse customers.
Priya K: Can you paste the example so we can see the exact math?
Sam D: Heres the snippet the PR currently has:
```
Example request: generate 350 tokens + 2 embeddings
Doc math: generation = 350 * $0.000025 = $0.00875
embeddings = 2 * $0.00035 = $0.00070
Total = $0.00945
```
This ignores that the customer is on a Dedicated reserved contract where generation gets a 15% reserved discount and token rounding is per-request.
Victor B: Oof. Also our billing pipeline emits separate meter events: `generation.tokens` and `embeddings.units`. The Console groups things by SKU on the Billing page, so readers might assume a single combined SKU.
Jules (docs): Suggested replacement: make the worked example explicit about list vs post-discount prices and call out rounding. Proposed text: 
```
Worked example (illustrative):
Request: generate 350 tokens + 2 embeddings
List price: generation = 350 tokens * $0.000025/token = $0.00875
List price: embeddings = 2 * $0.00035/embed = $0.00070
List subtotal = $0.00945
Reserved discount (generation only, example 15%): discounted generation = $0.00875 * 0.85 = $0.0074375
Total after discount = $0.0074375 + $0.00070 = $0.0081375 (~$0.00814)
Note: Tokens are rounded per request to the nearest token unit; final billed values may differ slightly due to meter aggregation and rounding policies.
```
Can we also add a tiny SDK sample to help engineers map requests to meter events?
Sam D: Sure, Python sample: 
```py
# python example (requests)
resp = client.responses.create(
  model='rw-instruct-1',
  input='Please summarize...',
  # embeddings call submitted in same logical flow
  embeddings={'model':'rw-embed-1','inputs':['...','...']}
)
# Billing records: generation.tokens -> 350, embeddings.units -> 2
```
Priya K: Id add that plus a 3-row matrix in the docs clarifying which discounts apply where: Hosted (no reserved), Dedicated (reserved applies to generation in examples), Private (contract-dependent). Keep it short.
Jules (docs): I'll update the heading to "Mixed-workload billing example" and add a pointer to the metering glossary for `token` and `embedding unit`. Also will include a small Console screenshot showing the two-panel split (generation vs embeddings) to reduce confusion.
BillingBot: CI status - docs/build: succeeded (https://ci.internal.redwood/docs/8992) :white_check_mark:
Victor B: One tiny nit: change the illustrative discount to 10% instead of 15% so we're conservative in examples.
Sam D: Done. Updated the PR with 10% example and the Python snippet. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/8992 :eyes: 
Jules (docs): Reviewing now. If CI stays green Ill merge and backport the wording into the billing FAQ. Thanks all :thumbsup:
